subject: mathematics

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.107, chapter 9 TRIGONOMETRIC EQUATIONS, Short Answer question 1(iv). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 shape gives a separate mark to the range check, because sinθ = 5 is the whole point of this question — a student who factorises correctly and then writes an angle for sinθ = 5 has lost the question, not a detail. Nothing is squared and no denominator is cleared here, so sinθ = 5 is a genuine out-of-range root, not an extraneous one, and the card says which of the two it is. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Equations supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Convert to one ratio
steps.margin_note: First mark. The equation mixes cos² with sin, so replace cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ. Then bring every term to the left so sin²θ carries a positive coefficient.
steps.memory_tip: cos² with a plain sin means one substitution: cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ. Then collect on the side where sin²θ stays positive.

recall.must_convey: That cos²θ becomes 1 − sin²θ and the equation collects to 2sin²θ − 11 sinθ + 5 = 0.
accept: replace cos squared by one minus sin squared so the equation is two sin squared minus eleven sin plus five equals zero
convert to sine only and collect the terms
it becomes a quadratic in sine with a positive sin squared term
cos square ni one minus sin square ga marchi quadratic rasali
get everything into sine first

steps.why: An equation holding two different ratios cannot be factorised. Reducing it to sine alone turns it into a quadratic that any student can handle.
common_mistakes: Replacing sin²θ instead and leaving a cosine behind.
Sign slip when multiplying out the −2.

steps.label: Factorise the quadratic
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The product is 2 × 5 = 10 and the sum is −11, so split the middle term as −10 sinθ − sinθ.
steps.memory_tip: Product 10, sum −11: split the middle term as −10 sinθ − sinθ, and the bracket (sinθ − 5) is shared.

accept: split the middle term and factorise to two sin theta minus one into sin theta minus five
the factors are two sin minus one and sin minus five
treat sin theta as one unknown and factorise
middle term split chesi factorise cheyyali
factor the quadratic into two brackets

steps.why: Treating sinθ as a single unknown is what makes the factorisation ordinary. Nothing trigonometric happens in this line at all.
common_mistakes: Looking for factors of 11 instead of factors of 2 × 5 = 10.
Splitting the middle term as −5 sinθ − 6 sinθ, whose product is 30, not 10.

steps.label: Reject the impossible root
steps.margin_note: Third mark. sinθ = 5 lies outside [−1, 1], so that branch has no angle at all. Write the reason on the page — the mark is for the reason, not for crossing the root out.
steps.memory_tip: sinθ = 5 is outside [−1, 1], so it has no angle. Write the reason, do not just cross it out.

recall.must_convey: That sinθ = 5 is rejected because |sinθ| ≤ 1, with the reason stated.
accept: sin theta equals five is impossible because a sine never goes above one
reject the second root, the sine range is minus one to one
that branch has no angle since five is bigger than one
sin theta five impossible, sine range minus one to one
discard the impossible value and say why
heard_as: mod sin theta less than one

steps.why: A quadratic always gives two roots, but a trigonometric equation only accepts values a sine can actually take. Checking the range is part of solving, not a formality.
common_mistakes: Carrying sinθ = 5 forward and inventing an angle for it.
Discarding it with no reason given.

steps.label: Solve the valid root
steps.margin_note: Last mark. sinθ = 1/2 is sin(π/6), so the principal value is π/6 and the sine general solution applies. Keep n ∈ Z.
steps.memory_tip: sinθ = 1/2 = sin(π/6), so use the sine form nπ + (−1)ⁿ(π/6).
lines: Here the principal value is α = π/6
For sinθ = sinα, θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ α

recall.must_convey: That sinθ = 1/2 gives principal value π/6 and general solution θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(π/6), n ∈ Z.
accept: sin theta is a half which is sin pi by six so theta is n pi plus minus one to the n pi by six
the principal value is pi by six and the sine general solution follows
the answer is n pi plus minus one power n pi by six
sin theta half ante sin pi by six, general solution rasta
write the general solution for the valid root

steps.why: Only one branch survived, so there is one family of solutions — but it is still an infinite family, which is why n ∈ Z has to appear.
common_mistakes: Giving only θ = π/6 and no general solution.
Using the cosine general solution 2nπ ± α.
